intro: You've searched for a project management surveyor near you, which suggests you're planning a building project and need someone local to oversee it. A project management surveyor can manage contractors, programme, quality and budget on your behalf, so you're not left coordinating everything yourself. Finding the right one starts with knowing what to ask and what to look for.
need_heading: What people searching for a project management surveyor near me usually need
need_lead: Most people looking for a project management surveyor near them are about to start building work and want someone local to keep the project on track.
needs: You're extending your home and want a surveyor to manage the builder, the schedule and the budget from start to finish.
You're converting a loft or renovating a property and need someone to coordinate different trades and check the quality of work.
You're a landlord planning works to a rental property and want a local surveyor to oversee contractors and keep costs under control.
You've had problems with a previous project running over time or over budget and want proper project management this time.
You're buying a property that needs significant work and want a surveyor to project manage the refurbishment after you complete.
context_heading: Why local knowledge and clear agreements matter
context: Choosing a project management surveyor near you means they can visit the site regularly without long travel, which helps with keeping an eye on progress and quality. Many surveyors are members of the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors (RICS), and RICS-regulated firms must follow professional standards, hold insurance and offer a complaints process. Chartered surveyors use the letters MRICS or FRICS after their name.

Before you appoint anyone, make sure you understand what they will do and how often they will report to you. Clear contracts reduce risk, and regular site meetings keep control. Agree reporting frequency and the scope of their project management role in writing so there are no surprises.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Describe the building project you're planning, including whether it's an extension, renovation, conversion or something else.
Say where the property is located so we can introduce you to a surveyor who works in your area.
Mention the current stage of the project, such as whether you have planning permission or are still at the design stage.
Explain what you want the surveyor to manage, for example contractors, budget, programme or quality checks.
Let us know if you already have contractors lined up or if you need help finding them as part of the project management.
Include any particular concerns you have, such as keeping to a tight schedule or managing costs carefully.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the project management surveyor
questions: What experience do you have managing projects similar to mine, such as domestic extensions or refurbishments?
How often will you visit the site and what reporting will I receive?
Will you handle the appointment of contractors and agree the contract terms on my behalf?
How do you monitor budget and programme, and what happens if costs start to rise?
Are you a member of RICS, and is your firm regulated by RICS?
What is your complaints procedure if I'm not happy with the service?

faqs.q: What does a project management surveyor do?
faqs.a: A project management surveyor runs building projects on your behalf, managing contractors, programme, quality and budget. They act as your representative to help keep the project on track and to your specification.

faqs.q: How do I find a project management surveyor near me?
faqs.a: You can search the RICS directory for chartered surveyors in your area, or ask iComply to introduce you to a suitable local professional. It's worth checking that they have experience with projects like yours and that you understand their scope of work.

faqs.q: Do I need a project management surveyor for a small building project?
faqs.a: For smaller projects you might not need full project management, but a surveyor can still help with contracts and quality checks. It depends on the complexity of the work and how much time you have to oversee it yourself.

faqs.q: What should I agree with the surveyor before work starts?
faqs.a: You should agree the scope of their role, how often they will visit the site, what reports you'll receive and how they will manage the budget and programme. Clear contracts reduce risk, so make sure everything is in writing.
